name: Business Weight Data Model
description: Layered data model for business weight scoring. Defines BusinessWeightMetrics (signal_frequency, author_seniority, channel_gravity, engagement_velocity) as mutable tracking state, a cached business_weight float on Context with default 0.5 and policy floor 0.1, an effective_business_weight property that enforces the floor, and a pure compute_business_weight function that aggregates metrics into a composite score clamped to [0.0, 1.0]. Backward compatible via Pydantic defaults — no migration needed for existing contexts. Metrics use 0.5 as the "no information available" sentinel. The effective weight is used for token budget allocation and routing priority.

types.name: BusinessWeightMetrics

fields.name: signal_frequency
fields.description: How frequently this context generates actionable signals. 0.0 = silent/no signals, 1.0 = highest observed frequency. Default 0.5 = no information available. Update trigger: on each new inbound message or signal event. Data source: message timestamp deltas within the context, normalized against global baseline.

fields.name: author_seniority
fields.description: Seniority/authority level of the primary author or identity in this context. 0.0 = unknown/lowest authority, 1.0 = highest authority. Default 0.5 = no information available. Update trigger: on identity resolution or identity metadata refresh. Data source: identity resolver component — maps author identity to a normalized seniority score.

fields.name: channel_gravity
fields.description: Learned importance of the channel/medium this context operates in, derived from historical response patterns. 0.0 = lowest gravity (e.g. noisy broadcast channel), 1.0 = highest gravity (e.g. direct executive channel). Default 0.5 = no information available. Update trigger: on response outcome feedback (was the response acted upon, ignored, escalated). Data source: response pattern tracker — exponential moving average of response engagement by channel.

fields.name: engagement_velocity
fields.description: Rate of change of engagement within this context — captures momentum/urgency. 0.0 = decelerating/stale, 1.0 = rapidly accelerating engagement. Default 0.5 = no information available. Update trigger: on each interaction event (message, reaction, follow-up). Data source: windowed derivative of interaction count over time, normalized to [0.0, 1.0].

types.description: Mutable Pydantic BaseModel tracking the four component metrics that feed into business weight computation. NOT frozen — metrics update over time as signals arrive. Each metric defaults to 0.5 (neutral/unknown sentinel). Lives in primitives/ alongside Context.

types.name: BusinessWeightConfig

fields.name: weight_signal_frequency
fields.description: Weight applied to signal_frequency in the weighted average. Must be non-negative.

fields.name: weight_author_seniority
fields.description: Weight applied to author_seniority in the weighted average. Must be non-negative.

fields.name: weight_channel_gravity
fields.description: Weight applied to channel_gravity in the weighted average. Must be non-negative.

fields.name: weight_engagement_velocity
fields.description: Weight applied to engagement_velocity in the weighted average. Must be non-negative.

fields.name: policy_floor
fields.description: Minimum effective business weight. The effective weight is max(computed_weight, policy_floor). Prevents any context from being starved of resources entirely.

types.description: Configuration for the business weight computation, including per-metric weights for the weighted average and the policy floor. Immutable once constructed. Lives alongside the compute function in core/business_weight.py.

types.name: BusinessWeightResult

fields.name: raw_weight
fields.description: The raw computed business weight from the weighted average of metrics, clamped to [0.0, 1.0]. This is stored on Context as business_weight.

fields.name: effective_weight
fields.description: The effective business weight after applying the policy floor: max(raw_weight, policy_floor). This is what token budget allocation and routing priority should use.

types.description: Result of a business weight computation, containing both the raw computed score and the effective (floor-applied) score.

types.name: MetricUpdateRequest

fields.name: signal_frequency
fields.description: New signal_frequency value, or None to leave unchanged.

fields.name: author_seniority
fields.description: New author_seniority value, or None to leave unchanged.

fields.name: channel_gravity
fields.description: New channel_gravity value, or None to leave unchanged.

fields.name: engagement_velocity
fields.description: New engagement_velocity value, or None to leave unchanged.

types.description: A request to update one or more component metrics on a BusinessWeightMetrics instance. Only non-null fields are applied (partial update semantics).

types.name: OptionalFloat
types.description: An optional float value — either a float or None.

types.name: MetricName
types.description: Enumeration of the four component metric names that feed into business weight.

functions.name: compute_business_weight
functions.description: Pure function that computes a composite business weight from component metrics using a weighted average formula. Located in core/business_weight.py. Formula: raw = clamp((w_sf * signal_frequency + w_as * author_seniority + w_cg * channel_gravity + w_ev * engagement_velocity) / sum_of_weights, 0.0, 1.0). Returns both raw and effective (floor-applied) weights. If all config weights are zero, returns default 0.5 as raw weight. This function has NO side effects — it does not mutate metrics or context.

inputs.name: metrics
inputs.description: The current component metrics for the context.

inputs.name: config
inputs.description: Configuration controlling per-metric weights and the policy floor. Defaults to equal weights (0.25 each) and floor 0.1.

error_cases.name: invalid_metric_value
error_cases.condition: Any metric value in metrics is outside [0.0, 1.0] (NaN or out of range)

error_data.field: name of the invalid metric field

error_cases.name: invalid_config_weight
error_cases.condition: Any weight value in config is outside [0.0, 1.0] or is NaN

error_data.field: name of the invalid config field

error_cases.name: invalid_policy_floor
error_cases.condition: config.policy_floor is outside [0.0, 1.0] or is NaN

preconditions: All metric values in metrics are in [0.0, 1.0]
All weight values in config are in [0.0, 1.0]
postconditions: If all config weights are zero, result.raw_weight == 0.5
If all metric values are equal to X, result.raw_weight == X (assuming non-zero weights exist)

functions.name: apply_metric_update
functions.description: Applies a partial metric update to a BusinessWeightMetrics instance, returning a new updated copy. Only fields present (non-None) in the update request are overwritten. This is a pure function — the original metrics instance is not mutated. Validates all provided values are in [0.0, 1.0] before applying.

inputs.name: current_metrics
inputs.description: The current metrics state to update from.

inputs.name: update
inputs.description: The partial update to apply. None fields are skipped.

error_cases.name: metric_value_out_of_range
error_cases.condition: A non-None value in update is outside [0.0, 1.0] or is NaN

error_data.field: name of the invalid metric field

preconditions: current_metrics is a valid BusinessWeightMetrics instance
All non-None values in update are in [0.0, 1.0]
postconditions: For each field in update that is not None, result.<field> == update.<field>
For each field in update that is None, result.<field> == current_metrics.<field>
All fields in result are in [0.0, 1.0]
The original current_metrics instance is not mutated

functions.name: get_effective_business_weight
functions.description: Convenience pure function that returns the effective business weight for a given raw business_weight value and policy floor. Equivalent to max(business_weight, policy_floor). This is the logic behind the effective_business_weight computed property on Context.

inputs.name: business_weight
inputs.description: The raw cached business weight from Context. Expected in [0.0, 1.0].

inputs.name: policy_floor
inputs.description: The policy floor to enforce. Defaults to 0.1.

error_cases.name: business_weight_out_of_range
error_cases.condition: business_weight is outside [0.0, 1.0] or is NaN

error_cases.name: policy_floor_out_of_range
error_cases.condition: policy_floor is outside [0.0, 1.0] or is NaN

functions.name: create_default_metrics
functions.description: Factory function that creates a BusinessWeightMetrics instance with all metrics set to the neutral default (0.5). Used when initializing a new context or when backward-compatible deserialization needs a default metrics object.

functions.name: validate_metrics
functions.description: Validates that all fields in a BusinessWeightMetrics instance are within the valid range [0.0, 1.0] and are not NaN. Returns True if valid, raises on invalid. Useful for defensive checks before computation.

error_cases.name: metric_out_of_range
error_cases.condition: Any metric field value is outside [0.0, 1.0]

error_data.field: name of the invalid metric field

error_cases.name: metric_is_nan
error_cases.condition: Any metric field value is NaN

error_data.field: name of the NaN metric field

postconditions: If function returns, result is True
All fields of metrics are in [0.0, 1.0] and are not NaN

invariants: All four component metrics (signal_frequency, author_seniority, channel_gravity, engagement_velocity) are always in [0.0, 1.0]
The default value for all component metrics is 0.5 (neutral/no-information sentinel)
The raw business_weight cached on Context is always in [0.0, 1.0] with default 0.5
The effective_business_weight is always max(business_weight, policy_floor) where policy_floor defaults to 0.1
effective_business_weight >= 0.1 under default configuration — no context is fully starved
compute_business_weight is a pure function: same inputs always produce same outputs, no side effects

Backward compatibility: existing Context instances without business_weight or business_weight_metrics deserialize successfully using Pydantic field defaults (business_weight=0.5, business_weight_metrics=BusinessWeightMetrics())
No migration scripts or schema version changes are required — this is a purely additive change
When all config weights are zero, compute_business_weight returns raw_weight=0.5 (the neutral default) to avoid division by zero
BusinessWeightMetrics is mutable (not frozen) — metrics are tracking state that updates over time
The sum of config weights need not equal 1.0 — the computation normalizes by dividing by the sum of weights
